text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 28-32 HRC."}],"comment":"The heat treatment specifies a hardness range but does not state the manufacturing stage at which it applies (e.g., before or after final machining). Without this, the machinist cannot plan the process sequence, risking distortion of finished features or inability to machine hardened stock. The designer should add the stage to the heat treatment callout in the title block or note N1.","recommended_correction":"Specify when the toughening is to be performed relative to machining operations, for example 'TO BE TOUGHENED TO 28-32 HRC AFTER ROUGH MACHINING, BEFORE FINISH MACHINING.'"},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D24","page":1,"quote":"⌀8   H7 THRU`"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"surface_treatment","page":1,"quote":"I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT)"}],"comment":"The ⌀8 H7 hole (D24) carries a tight fit tolerance, yet the part requires zinc plating (I.Z.B.P.) with no allowance made for the plating thickness on that bore. Plating buildup will reduce the hole diameter and cause the mating pin or fastener to fail to assemble. The designer should either mask the H7 bore during plating, specify that the H7 tolerance applies after plating, or open the pre-plate machining size to compensate for the coating thickness.","recommended_correction":"Add a note such as 'H7 TOLERANCE APPLIES AFTER PLATING' or 'MASK ⌀8 H7 HOLES DURING PLATING', or adjust the pre-plate hole size to account for the specified I.Z.B.P. coating thickness."}]}
